subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Hajj is which of the Five Pillars of Islam?
questions.explain: Hajj, the pilgrimage to Makkah, is the fifth of the Five Pillars of Islam.

questions.q: In which modern country is the city of Makkah located?
questions.explain: Makkah, the holiest city in Islam, lies in present-day Saudi Arabia.

questions.q: What is the name of the cube-shaped building at the centre of the Great Mosque in Makkah?
questions.explain: The Ka'bah is the cube-shaped structure towards which Muslims face in prayer.

questions.q: According to Islamic tradition, who rebuilt the Ka'bah?
questions.explain: Muslims believe the prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail rebuilt the Ka'bah as a house for the worship of one God.

questions.q: What is the name of the black cloth that covers the Ka'bah?
questions.explain: The Kiswah is the black embroidered cloth that drapes the Ka'bah and is replaced each year.

questions.q: What is the significance of the Ka'bah for Muslims during their daily prayers?
options: It is where sacrifices must be offered daily
It marks the qiblah, the direction Muslims face to pray
It is where the Qur'an is kept
It must be visited before every prayer
questions.explain: Muslims around the world face the Ka'bah, the qiblah, when performing their prayers.

questions.q: What is the name of the sacred stone set into a corner of the Ka'bah?
questions.explain: The Black Stone, or Hajar al-Aswad, is set in the eastern corner of the Ka'bah and pilgrims try to touch or point to it.

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar does the Hajj take place?
questions.explain: The Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.

questions.q: What is the name of the special state of purity and dress that pilgrims enter for the Hajj?
questions.explain: Ihram is the sacred state of ritual purity; men wear two plain white unstitched sheets.

questions.q: Why do male pilgrims wear two simple white unstitched cloths during the Hajj?
options: To keep cool in the desert climate
To symbolise the equality and unity of all pilgrims before God
To show which country they come from
To identify the leaders of each group
questions.explain: The identical simple garments remove signs of wealth and status, showing all are equal before Allah.

questions.q: What is the name of the ritual of walking seven times around the Ka'bah?
questions.explain: Tawaf is the circling of the Ka'bah seven times in an anti-clockwise direction.

questions.q: The Sa'i, walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, commemorates which event?
options: Hajar searching desperately for water for her son Ismail
Muhammad's flight from Makkah to Madinah
The building of the first mosque
questions.explain: The Sa'i re-enacts Hajar's frantic search for water, which ended when the Zamzam spring appeared.

questions.q: What is the name of the sacred well near the Ka'bah whose water pilgrims drink?
questions.explain: The Zamzam well is believed to have appeared miraculously to save Hajar and Ismail from thirst.

questions.q: What do pilgrims do while standing (wuquf) at Mount Arafat on the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah?
options: They pray, ask forgiveness and reflect until sunset
questions.explain: The standing at Arafat is a central rite where pilgrims pray for mercy and forgiveness; it is near where Muhammad gave his Farewell Sermon.

questions.q: What does the stoning of the pillars (Jamarat) at Mina symbolise?
options: The rejection of temptation and the devil
The end of the pilgrimage journey
questions.explain: Throwing pebbles at the pillars recalls Ibrahim rejecting the devil's temptations and represents casting away sin.

questions.q: The festival of sacrifice that takes place during the Hajj period is called:
questions.explain: Eid ul-Adha, the festival of sacrifice, commemorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God.

questions.q: A pilgrim collects small pebbles by night at Muzdalifah. Which ritual is she preparing to perform?
options: The stoning of the pillars at Mina
The Sa'i between Safa and Marwah
questions.explain: Pilgrims gather pebbles at Muzdalifah for the ritual stoning of the Jamarat pillars at Mina.

questions.q: An elderly Muslim has never made the Hajj because serious illness prevents her from travelling. According to Islamic teaching, what is her position?
options: She has committed a grave sin and cannot be forgiven
Hajj is only obligatory for those who are physically and financially able, so she is excused
She must send someone else in her place before she may pray again
She can no longer be considered a Muslim
questions.explain: The duty of Hajj applies only to Muslims who have the health and means to undertake it.

questions.q: Why is Makkah regarded as a sacred place by Muslims?
options: It is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and site of the Ka'bah
It is where the Prophet Musa received the law
It is the capital city of every Muslim country
It is where the Qur'an was first printed
questions.explain: Makkah is holy as Muhammad's birthplace and the home of the Ka'bah, the focus of Muslim prayer and pilgrimage.

questions.q: A Muslim describes how completing the Hajj made him feel his sins were forgiven and drew him closer to God. This best illustrates which purpose of visiting sacred places?
options: Spiritual renewal and a fresh start in one's relationship with God
Gaining political power in the community
Learning a new trade or profession
questions.explain: Pilgrimage to sacred places offers believers spiritual cleansing, forgiveness and renewed devotion to God.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Islam: Sacred Places & Pilgrimage
